baseline_construction: The five changed Windows runtime/renderer/native files are restored to 91cda3b; both variants use identical current benchmark instrumentation and Cargo features. Exact source and binary hashes are recorded.

single_window.method: Ten alternating process pairs; 20 samples per phase; per-process medians and 10000 paired bootstrap resamples; exact native captures; no working-set trimming.

experimental_three_window.method: Ten alternating process pairs; 20 samples per phase; per-process medians and 10000 paired bootstrap resamples; exact native captures; no working-set trimming.

earlier_long_run.applicability: Earlier candidate binaries, identified by their recorded hashes; not the final feature-gated binaries. Failed acceptance evidence is retained and is not a final-build stability pass.

earlier_heap_diagnostic.applicability: Earlier instrumented diagnostic binary; stable Rust allocation count is not a native-memory leak exclusion.

latency.method: Median of per-process p95 values; ten alternating independent process pairs; 10000 paired bootstrap resamples. Native messages, explicit repaint and DwmFlush; input foreground/focus and resulting content validated. Automation/frame-boundary latency, not a physical-keyboard end-to-end measurement.

adoption.default: Borrowed complete cache keys, exact-length geometry, borrowed paint text and paired buffered-paint lifetime; UIA empty replacement fix.
adoption.experimental: windows-font-sharing is opt-in and excluded from window/full; final-build long-run and compositor startup acceptance are not established.

limits: Windows runtime memory results do not estimate Linux/macOS memory savings.
Mixed-DPI 1.0/1.5/2.0 sharing is a core test, not a physical multi-monitor certification.
Window-ready timings are visibility proxies, not compositor first-frame latency.
A stable Rust live-allocation count does not prove that all native memory is leak-free.
